Yes—under those conditions, you would very likely be able to spot the Moon.

At an altitude of **21°** and azimuth **239°** (southwest), it is comfortably above the horizon, and a **37% illuminated** Moon is bright enough to stand out easily in a clear, dark sky. Its angular separation from the Sun, **75°**, also means it is well into the evening sky rather than lost in twilight; with the Sun nearly 50° below the horizon, sky brightness should not be a limiting factor.

Look roughly **southwest, 21° above the horizon**—about two fists held at arm’s length above the horizon, depending on your hand size. Nearby buildings, mountains, trees, haze, or urban light pollution could obstruct or wash it out, but if you have an unobstructed view, an ordinary observer should readily see it.
